Step 1 · Roast · gstack

LIVE

Let the AI grill your idea before you build it

# install: github.com/garrytan/gstack

/office-hours

An app where a mechanic photographs a part and gets

instructions on how to fix it.

You get: hard questions about who it’s for and why, then a design doc saved to the repo. No code.

Then: /plan-ceo-review asks whether this is even the right thing to build.

Step 2 · Plan · gstack

Turn the doc into a plan the agent can follow

/plan-eng-review

Stack: Next.js, shadcn/ui, Supabase, Vercel. Web app.

Architecture

Pages, API routes, tables

Data flow

Photo → model → manual page → job note

Edge cases

Blurry photo, no match

Test plan

What “done” means

Pick the stack yourself. Leaving it open might cause the agent to pick different stacks every time.

Step 2 · Make it visible

LIVE

See the plan before you build it

Create a visual artifact of what we just did with the

office hours and tech stack, please.

The idea

User, problem and scope from the roast

The stack

What runs where, and why

The flow

A diagram from photo to saved job note

The risks

Edge cases and the test plan

Why: nobody reads a 200-line plan. A one-page picture gets your team aligned in a minute, and it’s a ready-made slide for the judges.

Step 3 · Tasks

Break the plan into tasks

Break docs/eng-plan.md into small tasks, one PR each,

with acceptance criteria. Create them in Linear.

Linear

claude mcp add --transport http linear-server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp

GitHub Issues

Free, already next to your code. The agent uses gh issue create.

TASKS.md

Zero setup. A checklist in the repo the agent ticks off.

Step 4 · Build a task · Supabase MCP

Build the database

# connect the Supabase MCP to a dev project, then:

Create a jobs table (photo_url, part, manual_page, note,

user_id). Turn on RLS so users only see their own rows.

Add a storage bucket for photos.

Why RLS matters: Moltbook leaked about 1.5 million API keys because its public Supabase key shipped with RLS off. AI tools often skip it unless you ask.

Connect only the MCPs you need. Each one eats the agent’s context and can carry prompt-injection risk.

Step 4 · Build a task · pstack

LIVE

Implementing your tasks

/pstack:poteto-mode implement the Linear task “Save a job note”.

Work on a new branch and open a PR when it passes.

/how

Reads how the code works now

/architect

Sketches a few designs

Build + test

Writes the code and its tests

Verify

Checks it in the real app

Open PR

Ready for review

poteto-mode reads the task, picks the matching playbook (feature, bug fix, refactor) and runs every step. Never let an agent work straight on main.

Step 5 · PR review loop · pstack + /loop

LIVE

One agent reviews, another fixes

Reviewer · window 2

/pstack:interrogate the open PR.

Post the “blocking” findings as

review comments with gh.

Author · window 1

/loop check whether CI passed

and address any review comments

Re-checks on its own, fixes, pushes, replies. Save your standing rules in .claude/loop.md.

Blocking findings AI reviews always find nits/small issues with your PRs. For a hackathon, it's important to focus on the high priority, blocking findings.

Make it visible: ask for the findings as a one-page HTML report, or a Claude artifact.

Step 6 · Ship · GitHub + Vercel

Deploying for free

  1. One prompt deploys it and adds the PR check.
  2. Connect the repo in Vercel once: every PR gets a preview link.
  3. Merge only when the check is green.
  4. Merge to main and it’s live.

# with the Vercel MCP connected:

Deploy this app to Vercel and give

me the live URL.

Then add a GitHub Action that runs

npm run check on every pull request.

Bonus · Test it like a user

LIVE

Let the agent use your app

Look at it · your browser

# claude --chrome

Use my browser to go through

hackathon.ivanavr.com and test the

layouts from desktop down to small

phones. Screenshot anything broken.

Best for: spotting layout bugs by eye.

Prove it · Playwright

Write a Playwright test that clicks

through the main flow on desktop and

iPhone sizes. Record a video of each

run, then run it and show me.

Best for: a check that reruns on every PR.

Free bonus: that Playwright recording is your backup demo video for the judges.

Bonus · Polish your UI

Same page, one skill later

Before · first pass

After · taste-skill

npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill → “restyle this page with taste-skill”

judging

Tips to win

Problem first

Who hurts and how, before any tech.

Prioritize your main feature

One thing clearly working beats five half-built features.

Happy path working

Make sure your happy path and demo is working 100%.

No stalls

Mock slow calls, pre-fill forms, seed demo data.

Public URL

A localhost-only demo can score as if it doesn’t work.

Backup video

Record it early so there’s time to redo it.

The test: after one minute, could a judge explain your project, who it’s for, and why it needs AI?
